chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was approached and it was said to him: 'O Messenger of God, there has been a killing in Juhayna.' So the Messenger of God arose and walked until he reached their mosque. He said: The people heard (the news) and came to him. He said: 'Who killed this person?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, we do not know.'

So he said: 'A person killed among the Muslims and it is not known who killed him! By the One Who sent me with the Truth, if the inhabitants of the sky and the earth were to participate in the shedding of the blood of a Muslim person and were pleased with it, God would surely cast them headlong upon their nostrils into the Fire' — or he said: 'upon their faces.'

key_terms.جُهَيْنَةَ: Juhayna, an Arab tribe from the Hijaz region
key_terms.دَمِ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ: The blood of a Muslim person — a legal and ethical category denoting inviolable sanctity
key_terms.شَرِكُوا: Were complicit/participated — collective moral and legal responsibility
key_terms.قَتِيلٌ: One who has been slain; a murder victim
key_terms.لَأَكَبَّهُمُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنَاخِرِهِم: God would cast them headlong (on their nostrils) — a vivid idiom for utter humiliation and punishment
key_terms.وَالَّذِي بَعَثَنِي بِالْحَقِّ: By the One Who sent me with the Truth — the Prophet's characteristic oath formula

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the punishment for killing a Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a historical incident in which the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) was informed of an unresolved killing in the tribe of Juhayna. Walking personally to their mosque and gathering the community, the Prophet declared through a solemn oath that complicity in the unjust killing of even one Muslim — even if shared by all the inhabitants of heaven and earth — carries a punishment of being cast headlong into Hellfire. The oath formula 'By the One Who sent me with the Truth' is among the Prophet's strongest emphatic formulations, reflecting the absolute inviolability of Muslim blood. The variant ending ('upon their nostrils' or 'upon their faces') is a common form of hadith transmission preserving the narrator's honest uncertainty about the exact wording.
